There are **six quizzes**, given in class, taking approximately the first **25 minutes** of the session. Together they are worth 25% of your grade, and **the lowest is dropped** for students in both 4850 and 5850.

Policies --- logistics, accommodations, conflicts, and academic integrity --- are on the [quiz policies page](policies/quiz.qmd).

## Dates and Coverage

| Quiz | Date | Covers Through | Topics |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **Quiz 1** | Mon 2/08 | Fri 2/05 | Probability review, Monte Carlo |
| **Quiz 2** | Mon 2/22 | Fri 2/19 | Regression, the hinge, null models, both bootstraps |
| **Quiz 3** | Fri 3/05 | Fri 2/26 | The bootstrap in practice, Bayes, MCMC |
| **Quiz 4** | Fri 3/19 | Fri 3/12 | GLMs, maximum entropy, extremes: GEV and POT |
| **Quiz 5** | Fri 4/09 | Fri 3/26 | Thresholds, nonstationary extremes, time series |
| **Quiz 6** | Mon 5/03 | Fri 4/23 | Model evaluation and the criteria contrast |

::: {.callout-important}
## A Quiz Never Covers The Same Week

Every quiz covers material through the *previous* Friday at the latest, and nothing after it. This is a rule, not a tendency, and it is why the dates sit where they do. It also guarantees that there is always a homework assignment on the material, with its solution key in your hands, before the quiz that tests it.
:::

## What Is On A Quiz

The emphasis is on concepts. There is **no programming**, and **nothing requiring memorized formulas**. Expect 3--5 questions worth 1--3 points each, drawn from the same six forms the [homework assignments](homework.qmd) rehearse:

| Form | What it asks |
|:--|:--|
| **State the model with its assumptions** | Write out the equations, including *any and all* assumptions |
| **Define a property** | What does it mean for an estimator to be unbiased? |
| **Read a diagnostic** | Here is an ACF, a trace plot, a residual plot --- what does it tell you? |
| **Interpret a result** | Often as true/false statements about a reported interval |
| **Small computation** | How many Monte Carlo samples for a given standard error? |
| **State an assumption** | What does the non-parametric bootstrap assume? |

**The homework assignments are the sample quizzes.** That is what they are for, and it is why there is one before every quiz.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why Quizzes 1 and 2 Are On Mondays

Every other quiz is on a Friday. The first two cannot be, because the Fridays they would need --- 2/12, 2/19, and 2/26 --- hold the three sessions this course is built around, and none of them can afford to lose 25 minutes. Quiz 1 also needs to be early enough that you find out what a quiz looks like while it is still cheap, which rules out waiting for the next free Friday in March.
:::
